{{Quote|In its classical form, as transcribed by Homonix Rectonia during the Early Manderon Period, the Code consists of five core precepts ''[...]''.|Fae Coven, explaining the Jedi Code in ''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force''|<ref name="TJP" />}}
'''Homonix Rectonia''' was a member of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] during the early [[Manderon Period]],<ref name="TJP" /> which began in [[7000 BBY]].<ref name="Manderon Period">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> One of Rectonia's lasting contributions to the Order was the transcription of the [[Jedi Code/Legends|Jedi Code]] in its classical form. Consisting of five precepts, the Code would be modified and altered over the [[Millennium/Legends|millennia]]; however, following the [[Ruusan Reformations/Legends|Ruusan Reformation]] of [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]], Rectonia's original work was restored by [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] [[Fae Coven]] in ''[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force]]'', a [[Jedi training/Legends|Jedi trainee]] [[Book/Legends|guidebook]] that was still in use during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] almost a millennium later.<ref name="TJP" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|In the text, this version of the Jedi Code is mentioned as its "classical form," as transcribed by "Homonix Rectonia during the early Manderon Period." The mention that there are other&mdash;more controversial&mdash;versions of the Jedi Code is an acknowledgment of how ridiculously tangled Jedi lore would have to be after 25,000 years of growth.|Daniel Wallace|<ref name="Blog">{{Blogspot|subdomain=geekosity|url=2010/12/endnotes-for-star-wars-jedi-path-part-1.html|name=Daniel Wallace's Geekosity|text=Endnotes for Star Wars: The Jedi Path (part 1 of 4)}}</ref>}}
Homonix Rectonia was first mentioned in [[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force (real-life book)|''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force'']], a reference book written by [[Daniel Wallace]] and published in [[2010]].<ref name="TJP" /> In the endnotes for ''The Jedi Path'', Wallace told that he wanted to recognize the multiple interpretations of the Jedi Code that had existed during the Order's 25 millennia history, therefore establishing that Rectonia's transcription of the Code was considered its "classical" form.<ref name="Blog" /> The [[Canon|non-canon]] [[2014]] young readers book ''[[LEGO Star Wars: Yoda's Secret Missions]]'', written by [[Ace Landers]], mentioned that Rectonia transcribed the classical version of the code and that the Jedi was a [[Jedi Master/Legends|Master]].<ref name="Secret Missions">''[[LEGO Star Wars: Yoda's Secret Missions]]''</ref>
